newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania eleven-month current account gap $1.58 bln.
newsitem.headline: Romania eleven-month current account gap $1.58 bln.

text.p: Romania's current account deficit rose to $1.58 billion over January-November last year, compared to $1.32 billion in the same period of 1995, central bank data showed on Friday.
Latest statistics put Romania's trade balance deficit, in FOB prices, at $1.543 billion in 1996, but the figure does not include $216.3 million in oil imports delayed by customs procedures.
Romania's new centrist coalition government has pledged to slash the current account gap to $1.4 billion in 1997 from an estimated $2.3 billion last year.
The former leftist government's attempts to keep the local leu currency overvalued last year triggered a 3.2 percent fall in Romanian exports, widening the current account deficit.
The leu has sunk by some 120 percent to about 9,000 against the dollar since January 1.
